title: Political Theory: Nature, Evolution, and Traditional Approaches

scenes.text: Can politics ever be studied as a pure science like physics?
scenes.narration: Imagine trying to measure justice or freedom with a thermometer! For centuries, scholars have asked: is political science a search for scientific laws, or a moral guide for good life?

scenes.text: Cricket rulebooks set ideal standards, while match scorecards record what players actually do.
scenes.narration: Here is a simple analogy using cricket. The official rulebook prescribes how the game ought to be played fairly, but match statistics describe what players actually do on the pitch. Political theory studies both the ideals and the real game.

scenes.heading: Evolution of Political Science

events.what: Plato studies politics as ethical philosophy
Politics becomes part of religious scholastics
Behaviouralism attempts to build pure science

scenes.narration: Political science began in Ancient Greece as ethics. Later, Machiavelli made politics independent, American behaviouralists tried turning it into a pure laboratory science, and finally post-behaviouralists established it as an applied science.

scenes.heading: Four Traditional Approaches
items: Philosophical approach examines normative values like justice
Historical approach analyzes past contexts to understand ideas
Institutional approach studies constitutions and government organs
Empirical approach gathers observable facts through experience
scenes.narration: Before modern computers, scholars relied on four traditional approaches: philosophical ideals, historical context, legal institutions, and empirical observations of real political life.

scenes.heading: Textual Versus Contextual Approach
scenes.narration: How should we read classical texts? Contextualists in the Cambridge School argue that words change meaning over centuries, so we must understand the author's historical situation rather than just reading words literally.

scenes.heading: Normative Versus Empirical Approaches

columns.title: Normative Approach
items: Studies values like justice and liberty
Deals with what ought to be

scenes.narration: Here is the fundamental divide in political theory: normative theory asks what ought to be, prescribing moral ideals, while empirical theory observes what actually is, describing observable facts.

scenes.name: March and Olson
scenes.idea: Institutions, rules, and procedures constrain choices rather than individual behaviour alone.
scenes.narration: In modern political thought, March and Olson revived the institutional approach. They showed that human actors do not make choices in a vacuum; rules, norms, and procedures constantly shape their decisions.

items: Political science evolved from philosophy into an applied science
Traditional approaches combine normative ideals with empirical facts
Contextualism and new institutionalism revived historical and institutional methods
scenes.narration: Remember these three big takeaways: political science evolved toward an applied science, traditional approaches balance values with facts, and modern revivals keep history and institutions central to UPSC PSIR.
